data.content:
Book
A book is an item that can be borrowed, returned by its due date, and renewed if eligible.<SEP>Books can be borrowed and should be returned on or before their due dates.<SEP>The book can be renewed if nobody else has reserved it, or returned by its original due date if it is reserved.<SEP>A book is an item that a student may borrow, renew under stated conditions, and return by its own due date.<SEP>The book is the library item that may be renewed once for seven extra days if nobody else has reserved it.

Standard Loan Period
The guide's table lists the standard loan period.<SEP>The standard loan period is the baseline duration of a student book loan.

My Loans
My Loans is the interface where a borrower can find a book and request a renewal.<SEP>My Loans displays the due date for each borrowed book.<SEP>My Loans displays the book's new due date after renewal.<SEP>My Loans is where a student checks the due date for each book title.<SEP>My Loans is the library account area where a borrower finds a book and views its new due date after renewal.

Library Borrowing Guide
Library Borrowing Guide is the title of a guide about library borrowing.<SEP>The Library Borrowing Guide provides instructions for checking titles, returning books by their due dates, and requesting renewals.<SEP>The Library Borrowing Guide provides instructions for borrowing and returning books.<SEP>The Library Borrowing Guide provides instructions for renewing and returning a book.<SEP>The Library Borrowing Guide provides baseline student borrowing limits and instructions for checking eligibility, tracking due dates, renewing books, and returning them on time.

Account Eligibility
Account eligibility should be checked before borrowing.<SEP>Account eligibility must be checked before a student borrows a book.

Due Date
The due date is the deadline by which a borrowed book should be returned and before which a renewal should be requested.<SEP>The due date is displayed for each book and indicates when the book should be returned.<SEP>A due date is the individual return deadline for a borrowed book.<SEP>The due date is the date by which the book should be returned, and the updated due date should be checked after renewal.

Borrowing and Returning Books
Borrowing and returning books are the activities covered by the guide.

Loan Limit
The guide's table lists a limit for borrowing.

Account
The account's eligibility should be checked before borrowing.

Table
The table lists the borrowing limit and standard loan period.

Book Title
Each borrowed book title should be checked separately when borrowing several books.

Renewal
A renewal gives a borrower more time to keep a book; it can be requested once for seven extra days if nobody else has reserved the book.<SEP>Renewal is an option for a book that has not been reserved by someone else, and it extends the borrowing period by seven days.<SEP>A renewal may extend a book loan once for seven extra days, if completed before the due date and if nobody else has reserved the book.<SEP>Renewal is an action performed before the original due date; it is available once for seven extra days if the book has no reservation.

Reservation
A reservation by another person makes a book ineligible for the renewal described in the guide.<SEP>A reservation affects whether the book can be renewed or must be returned by the original due date.<SEP>A reservation by another person prevents renewal and means the book should be returned by its original due date.

Original Due Date
The original due date is the deadline for returning a reserved book.<SEP>The original due date is the deadline by which a reserved book must be returned and before which a renewal should be requested.

Seven Extra Days
Seven extra days is the length of the extension provided by the described renewal.<SEP>Seven extra days is the extension period available for an eligible book renewal.<SEP>Seven extra days is the additional loan period available after an eligible renewal.

New Due Date
The new due date is displayed in My Loans after the book is renewed.<SEP>The new due date is the updated return deadline shown in My Loans after a successful renewal.

Renewal Steps
Renewal Steps are identified as Figure 1 in the guide.<SEP>The renewal steps are to check the due date, find the book in My Loans, renew the book, and check the resulting due date.

Title
A title is an identifying name that the guide instructs borrowers to check separately.

Due Date Check
The guide instructs borrowers to check the date again before returning the book.

data.entity_name: Student Book Borrowing Limits and Standard Loan Period (table)
data.content: The table states that students may borrow a maximum of 3 books at a time, with a standard loan period of 14 days. It supplies the baseline rules for the Library Borrowing Guide; surrounding instructions explain checking individual due dates in My Loans and the conditional option to renew once for 7 extra days.

A three-card, left-to-right flow diagram showing the library renewal steps: check the due date, find the book in My Loans, and renew while checking the new due date. It supports the guide’s instructions to renew before the due date and verify the updated return date.

14 Days
Fourteen days is the standard loan period for student borrowing.

3 Books
Three books is the maximum number of books a student may borrow at a time.

Student
A student is the borrower subject to the borrowing rules described in the Library Borrowing Guide.

Maximum Books At A Time
Maximum books at a time is the borrowing quantity limit specified for students.

Book Reservation
A reservation by another person prevents a student from renewing the reserved book under the stated instructions.

7 Extra Days
Seven extra days is the extension available through an eligible one-time renewal.

Figure 1
Figure 1 is a diagram illustrating the ordered steps for renewing a library book.
